paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Day of the LORD is no small thing. Joel pictures darkness, an army nothing can stop, and then asks, "Who can endure it?" (Joel 2:11). He wants you to take it seriously, because the LORD is the One at the head of that army.

But look at what comes right after that heavy question. "Yet even now," declares the LORD, "return to Me with all your heart" (Joel 2:12). Even now! The door is still open, and He wants a torn heart, not torn clothes (Joel 2:13). I think a heart is a lot harder to tear than an apron, and I would know, because I've been through that drawer.

So why come back? Because He is "gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion" (Joel 2:13). Joel says, "Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him" (Joel 2:14). That's why the ram's horn blows again, and this time it calls everybody together to return to Him (Joel 2:15-16). If you've drifted, friend, don't wait for a better day to come back. The LORD is calling you home right now, and my ovens are staying ready.
